description:
Programme or Project Overview

Lund University invites applications for a doctoral student in industrial design with a focus on strategic design. The project examines design as a strategic resource in organisations and society, studying how design competence shapes decision-making, innovation processes and long-term organisational direction. The doctoral student will investigate how strategic design is practised in real organisations, develop conceptual frameworks, and contribute to the academic conversation on design's expanding role beyond products and services.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral employment within Lund University's design research environment, which combines practice-led design research with social-science perspectives. The doctoral student will combine case studies, interviews and possibly practice-based work, collaborate with partner organisations, and publish in international design and management research venues. The environment supports experimentation and welcomes applicants from both design practice and design research backgrounds.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in industrial design, design or a related field, with a demonstrable interest in how design operates at strategic and organisational levels. Professional design experience, workshop facilitation skills or familiarity with qualitative research methods are advantages. Applications are submitted through Lund University's Varbi portal with a portfolio or examples of design work, a CV, transcripts, references and a statement of research interests.

Highlights

  • Salaried four-year PhD in industrial design at Lund University
  • Strategic design as a resource in organisations and society
  • Case studies with partner organisations
  • Practice-led design research environment
  • International publication and collaboration opportunities
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system
